stories.title: Google says AI search earns less, plans to add more ads
stories.summary: Google acknowledged AI-powered search generates less revenue than traditional search and said it will add more ads to compensate, after posting a $9.06 billion negative cash flow.
stories.more: The admission came alongside Google's Q3 earnings report. Negative cash flow reportedly ballooned to $9.06 billion. Google's stock price fell following the earnings release, and the company says increasing ad load is part of its plan to offset AI search's lower monetization.

items.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
items.excerpt: Google's negative cash flow balloons to -$9.06 billion, and stock price tumbles following Q3 earnings.

stories.title: Ex-Palantir execs raise $17M for construction AI world models
stories.summary: Dream, a startup founded by former Palantir employees, raised $17 million from a16z to build AI world models aimed at disrupting Autodesk in construction.
stories.more: The startup trained its models on data from 100 million square feet of building permits. It aims to compete with incumbent construction software maker Autodesk using AI world models.

items.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
items.excerpt: rained on 100 million square feet of building permits, dream wants to disrupt Autodesk with AI.

stories.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees amid AI push
stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the US, UK, and Canada, a sign CEO Satya Nadella's AI strategy is reshaping the company's workforce.
stories.more: The buyout offer follows years of Nadella signaling that AI would change the size of Microsoft's workforce. It spans roughly 60,000 employees across the US, UK, and Canada. The move is read as one of the clearest signals yet that Microsoft expects AI to reduce headcount needs going forward.

items.excerpt: To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft's workforce. stories.title: AI app-building agent Wabi raises $55M at $1.25B valuation

stories.more: The round was announced Thursday. Wabi has repositioned itself from an app-building tool to describing itself as a personal agent.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing bets everything on compute spending
stories.summary: Anthropic filed an S-1 to go public on the Nasdaq, with analysts reading the filing as justification for massive, continued compute spending toward AGI.
stories.more: The S-1 filing lays out Anthropic's financials ahead of its Nasdaq listing. On The Verge's Decoder podcast, SemiAnalysis analyst Joey Brookhart discussed the numbers behind the filing. A separate Verge analysis argues the document provides Anthropic's financial case for spending as much as possible on compute. Coverage frames the filing as evidence the company is betting big on reaching AGI while presenting itself to investors as a product business.

stories.summary: Chinese AI labs are increasingly using OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model instead of Claude, after Anthropic tightened restrictions on its models.
stories.more: The shift follows Anthropic tightening its defenses against use by Chinese AI labs. GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's most powerful model, has become their main target as a result.

stories.title: Deepgram acquires Pipecat-maker Daily for voice AI infrastructure
stories.summary: Voice AI company Deepgram acquired Daily, maker of the open-source Pipecat framework, to strengthen its real-time voice infrastructure.
stories.more: The deal gives Deepgram deeper capabilities in real-time voice and video infrastructure through Daily's Pipecat technology.

items.title: Deepgram acquires Pipecat-maker Daily to bolster its voice AI infrastructure

stories.title: Startup &Truth bets on formal verification to make AI coding safer
stories.summary: A new startup called &Truth is using formal verification, a math-based method for proving software correctness, to address risks in AI-generated 'vibe coding.'
stories.more: Formal verification is described as a painstaking process that uses mathematical proofs to show software behaves as intended. &Truth joins a growing race of companies applying this approach to AI-assisted coding as a response to the safety concerns it raises.

items.title: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
items.excerpt: A new startup called &Truth is joining the race to automate formal verification, a painstaking process that uses math to prove software works as intended.

stories.title: Simon Willison quotes Ben Hylak's dig at headless-MCP hype
stories.summary: Simon Willison highlighted a quip from Ben Hylak joking that every other product should become a headless MCP server feeding an agent, except the one he's selling.
stories.more: Hylak's quote pokes at a common pattern in AI tool pitches: companies want competitors' products reduced to headless MCP integrations while insisting users will still love their own product's UI. Willison shared it without additional commentary.

items.title: Quoting Ben Hylak
items.excerpt: every product i use should just be a headless mcp, that feeds into an agent, where i never have to think about anything underneath. except for our product, of course. in our product, customers love the ui and love us very much. we're special that way. — Ben Hylak Tags: model-context-protocol , ai

stories.title: Mistral releases Large 4 'Le Chonk' with open weights
stories.summary: Mistral open-sourced the weights of Large 4 ('Le Chonk'), a 1-trillion-parameter model it calls the best open-weight model for coding, trained entirely in Europe.
stories.more: The model is multimodal and was trained entirely in Europe. Mistral says it beats other open-weight models at coding and cybersecurity, and claims it has leapfrogged Chinese labs in the open-weight race on those fronts. Independent testing cited by The Decoder found it fast and comparatively cheap to run. On that outlet's benchmark it scored 26 points, behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3, which both scored 32, so it still trails China's top models overall. The release drew over 500 points and 130+ comments on Hacker News within hours.

items.title: Le Chonk: Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders.
items.excerpt: The weights of Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) are now open. A 1T parameter multimodal model, and best open-weight model for coding, trained in Europe.

items.title: Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race
items.excerpt: The French AI lab claims its latest release matches or outperforms even the best models from DeepSeek and Z.ai in coding and cybersecurity.

items.title: Paris-based Mistral releases "Le Chonk," a strong coding model that still trails China overall
items.excerpt: Mistral has released the weights for Large 4, aka "Le Chonk," a trillion-parameter model trained entirely in Europe. Mistral says it beats its open rivals at coding, and independent testing shows it's fast and fairly cheap. It still can't match China's top models, scoring 26 points to the 32 posted by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3. stories.title: Elorian's Glimpse benchmark tests if models can see past decoys
stories.summary: A new 'decoy counting' benchmark from Elorian, called Glimpse, exposes a gap between frontier models' visual perception and reasoning, and tries to close it by having models 'think with images.'
stories.more: The benchmark is built around decoy counting tasks that separate raw visual perception from downstream reasoning. Elorian's Glimpse approach has models reason while directly working with images, rather than converting them to text first.

items.title: Can Frontier Models See Past a Decoy? Elorian Tests Visual Reasoning
items.excerpt: A new decoy counting benchmark exposes a gap between seeing and reasoning. Elorian’s Glimpse tries to bridge it by thinking with images.

stories.title: RealCLI benchmark evaluates human-agent collaboration in CLI agents
stories.summary: A new paper introduces RealCLI, a benchmark that evaluates both task completion and collaboration quality for AI agents operating in command-line interfaces.
stories.more: Existing CLI agent benchmarks either assume fixed instructions throughout a task or judge only final outcomes, without capturing collaboration quality during execution. RealCLI pairs task execution evaluation with a five-dimensional framework for measuring human-agent collaboration on realistic CLI tasks.

items.title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
items.excerpt: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality.
